final_answer: Yes, SLE-associated immune cell changes differ between patients of Asian and European ancestry for two cell types. CD4-positive alpha-beta T cells show a significantly stronger depletion in Asian SLE patients (log2FC = −0.94) compared to European American patients (log2FC = −0.35; interaction FDR = 5.8×10⁻⁵, partial η² = 0.079, medium effect). Conversely, plasmacytoid dendritic cells exhibit a much stronger depletion in European American SLE patients (log2FC = −0.99) than in Asian patients (log2FC = −0.18; interaction FDR = 9.3×10⁻⁴, partial η² = 0.055, small effect). The remaining nine cell types (classical monocyte, B cell, CD8+ T cell, NK cell, non-classical monocyte, lymphocyte, conventional dendritic cell, plasmablast, and progenitor cell) showed no significant ancestry-dependent differences in their SLE-associated proportion changes. These findings suggest that the immunological footprint of SLE is partially ancestry-dependent, with CD4+ T-cell lymphopenia being a more prominent feature in Asian patients and pDC depletion more characteristic of European American patients.
